answer: A harbor ledger trusts only keys that have actually met people: each new identity must collect encounter receipts from five distinct established agents, exchanged over Bluetooth at gatherings within seven days, each bound to the epoch seed and a knoll location hash. A farm running 1,000 fakes needs 5,000 separate in-person meetings, each costing travel and a real human's time, while one honest agent finishes in an afternoon. The nectar is that encounters cannot be batched: the same pair may vouch only once per epoch, receipts are published for audit, and identical timestamps forfeit the bond.
